readings.title: A Message to the Land of Kush
readings.subtitle: A Present Brought to YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Isaiah 18:1] Woe to the land shadowed with whirring wings, which is beyond the rivers of Kush, [2] which sends envoys by sea, even in vessels of reed on the waters, saying, “Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people dreaded from their beginning onward, a nation mighty and trampling, whose land the rivers divide.” [3] All inhabitants of the world, and you that dwell on the earth: When a banner is lifted up on the mountains, look! And when a shophar is blown, hear! [4] For thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am still, and <dn>I</dn> watch in <dn>My</dn> dwelling place like dazzling heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”</dq> [5] <dq>For before harvest, when the bud is perfect and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, then <dn>He</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> the twigs with pruning hooks, and shall cut down and take away <dn>את</dn> the spreading branches.</dq> [6] <dq>They are left together for the mountain birds of prey and for the beasts of the earth. And the birds of prey shall summer on them, and all the beasts of the earth winter on them.</dq> [7] In that time a present shall be brought to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, and from a people awesome from their beginning onward – a nation mighty and trampling, whose land the rivers have divided – to the place of the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, to Mount Tsiyon.

readings.title: The Message Concerning Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: Judgment on Idols, Society, and Nature
readings.text: [Isaiah 19:1] The message concerning Mitsrayim. See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is riding on a swift cloud, and <dn>He</dn> shall come into Mitsrayim. And the idols of Mitsrayim shall tremble at <dn>His</dn> presence, and the heart of Mitsrayim melt in its midst. [2] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall stir up Mitsrites against Mitsrites, and they shall fight, each one against his brother, and each one against his neighbour, city against city, reign against reign.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the spirit of Mitsrayim shall vanish within them, and <dn>I</dn> destroy <dn>את</dn> their counsel. And they shall seek the idols and the mutterers, the mediums and the sorcerers.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall deliver <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites into the hand of a cruel master, and a fierce sovereign to rule over them,”</dq> declares the <dn>Master</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [5] And waters shall fail from the sea, and the river wasted and dried up. [6] And the rivers shall stink, and the streams shall be weak and dried up. Reeds and rushes shall wither. [7] Bare places by the River, by the mouth of the River, and every sown field by the River shall wither. It shall be driven away, and be no more. [8] And the fishermen shall lament, and all those who cast hooks into the River shall mourn, and they who spread nets on the waters shall pine away. [9] And those who work in fine flax, and those who weave fine fabric shall become ashamed. [10] And its foundations shall be crushed, all the wage workers grieved in being.

readings.title: The Folly of Mitsrayim's Princes
readings.subtitle: The Fear of Yehuḏah
readings.text: [Isaiah 19:11] The princes of Tso‛an are only fools; the counsel of Pharaoh’s wise ones has become senseless. How do you say to Pharaoh, “I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient sovereigns?” [12] Where are they? Where are your wise men? Let them show you, and let them know what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has counselled against Mitsrayim. [13] The princes of Tso‛an have become fools, the princes of Noph are deceived. They, the corner-stone of her tribes, have led <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim astray. [14] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has mixed a perverse spirit in her midst. And they have led <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim astray in all her work, as a drunkard strays in his vomit. [15] And there is no work for Mitsrayim, by either head or tail, palm branch or bulrush. [16] In that day Mitsrayim shall become like women, and tremble and fear because of the waving of the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, which <dn>He</dn> waves over it. [17] And the land of Yehuḏah shall be a fear to Mitsrayim, everyone who mentions it fears for himself, because of the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts which <dn>He</dn> has counselled against it.

readings.title: The Conversion of Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: A Highway from Mitsrayim to Ashshur
readings.text: [Isaiah 19:18] In that day five cities in the land of Mitsrayim shall speak the language of Kena‛an and swear by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts; one is called the City of Destruction. [19] In that day a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be in the midst of the land of Mitsrayim, and a standing column to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at its border. [20] And it shall be for a sign and for a witness to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts in the land of Mitsrayim. When they cry to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of the oppressors, <dn>He</dn> sends them a Saviour and an <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall deliver them. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be known to Mitsrayim, and the Mitsrites shall know <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in that day, and make slaughtering and meal offering, and shall make a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and pay it. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall smite <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim, smite it and heal it. And they shall turn to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall hear them and heal them. [23] In that day there shall be a highway from Mitsrayim to Ashshur, and Ashshur shall come into Mitsrayim and Mitsrayim into Ashshur, and Mitsrayim shall serve with Ashshur. [24] In that day Yisra’ěl shall be one of three with Mitsrayim and Ashshur, even a blessing in the midst of the earth, [25] whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts shall bless, saying, <dq>“Blessed is Mitsrayim <dn>My</dn> people, and Ashshur the work of <dn>My</dn> hands, and Yisra’ěl <dn>My</dn> inheritance.”</dq>

readings.title: Isaiah's Symbolic Act
readings.subtitle: A Sign Against Mitsrayim and Kush
readings.text: [Isaiah 20:1] In the year that Tartan came to Ashdoḏ, when Sargon the sovereign of Ashshur sent him, and he fought against Ashdoḏ and took it, [2] at that same time <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke by means of Yeshayahu son of Amots, saying, <dq>“Go, and remove <dn>את</dn> the sackcloth from your body, and take <dn>את</dn> your sandals off your feet.”</dq> And he did so, walking naked and barefoot. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“As <dn>My</dn> servant Yeshayahu has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder against Mitsrayim and Kush,</dq> [4] <dq>so does the sovereign of Ashshur lead away <dn>את</dn> the captives of Mitsrayim and <dn>את</dn> the exiles of Kush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered – the shame of Mitsrayim.</dq> [5] <dq>“And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Kush, their expectation, and of Mitsrayim, their boast.</dq> [6] <dq>“And the inhabitant of this coastland shall say in that day, ‘See, such is our expectation, wherever we flee for help to be delivered from the sovereign of Ashshur. And how do we escape?’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Message Concerning the Wilderness of the Sea
readings.subtitle: Baḇel is Fallen
readings.text: [Isaiah 21:1] The message concerning the Wilderness of the Sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep on, so it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land. [2] A distressing vision is revealed to me: the treacherous betrays, and the ravager ravages. Go up, O Ěylam! Besiege, O Media! All the groaning <dn>I</dn> bring to an end. [3] Therefore my loins are filled with anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labour. I was distressed when I heard it; I was troubled when I saw it. [4] My heart reeled, horror overwhelmed me; the night for which I longed <dn>He</dn> turned into fear for me. [5] Prepare the table, spread the mat, eat and drink. Arise, you princes, anoint <dn>את</dn> the shield! [6] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said this to me, <dq>“Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he sees.”</dq> [7] And he saw a chariot with a pair of horsemen, a chariot of donkeys, and a chariot of camels, and he listened attentively, very attentively. [8] Then he cried, <dq>“A lion, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and I have sat at my post every night.</dq> [9] <dq>“And see this, a chariot of men coming with a pair of horsemen!”</dq> And he spoke up and said, <dq>“Baḇel is fallen, is fallen! And all the carved images of her mighty ones <dn>He</dn> has broken to the ground.”</dq> [10] Oh, my threshing and the grain of my floor! That which <dn>I</dn> have heard from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dn>I</dn> have declared to you.

readings.title: The Message Concerning Dumah
readings.subtitle: The Watchman's Report
readings.text: [Isaiah 21:11] The message concerning Dumah. <dn>He</dn> calls to me out of Sě‛ir, “Watchman, how much of the night is passed? Watchman, how much of the night has passed?” [12] The watchman said, “Morning came, and also the night. If you inquire, inquire. Come again!”

readings.title: The Message Concerning Araḇia
readings.subtitle: The Fall of Qěḏar
readings.text: [Isaiah 21:13] The message concerning Araḇia. In the forest in Araḇia you stay, O you travelling companies of Deḏanites. [14] You who dwell in the land of Těma, bring water to him who is thirsty, meet the fugitive with bread. [15] For they fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the stress of battle. [16] For thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to me, <dq>“Within a year, according to the year of a hired man, all the esteem of Qěḏar shall come to an end,</dq> [17] <dq>and the rest of the number of archers, the mighty men of the people of Qěḏar, shall be few. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl has spoken.”</dq>

readings.title: The Message Concerning the Valley of Vision
readings.subtitle: A Rebuke for Frivolity
readings.text: [Isaiah 22:1] The message concerning the Valley of Vision. What troubles you now, that you have all gone up to the house-tops, [2] you who are filled with turmoils, a noisy city, a city of revelry? Your slain are not slain with the sword, nor the dead in battle. [3] All your rulers have fled together; without a bow they were taken captive. All who are found in you are bound together, who have fled from afar. [4] Therefore I said, “Look away from me, let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me because of the ravaging of the daughter of my people.” [5] For it is a day of uproar and treading down and perplexity by the <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts in the Valley of Vision – breaking down of a wall and of crying to the mountain. [6] And Ěylam bore the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Qir bared the shield. [7] And it shall be that your choicest valleys shall be filled with chariots, and the horsemen shall take up positions at the gate. [8] Then <dn>He</dn> removed <dn>את</dn> the covering of Yehuḏah. And you looked in that day to the weapons of the House of the Forest. [9] And you saw <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the city of Daviḏ, that it was great. And you gathered together the waters of the lower pool. [10] And you counted <dn>את</dn> the houses of Yerushalayim, and the houses you broke down to strengthen <dn>את</dn> the wall. [11] And you dug a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you have not looked to its Maker, nor have you seen <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> who fashioned it long ago. [12] And in that day the <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts called for weeping and for mourning, for baldness and for girding with sackcloth. [13] Then see! Joy and gladness, killing oxen and slaying sheep, eating meat and drinking wine, <dq>“Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”</dq> [14] And it was revealed in my hearing by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“For this crookedness shall certainly not be pardoned until you die,”</dq> said the <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: Judgment on Sheḇnah and Promotion of Elyaqim
readings.subtitle: The Key of the House of Daviḏ
readings.text: [Isaiah 22:15] Thus said the <dn>Master</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Go, come to this steward, to Sheḇnah, who is over the house, and say,</dq> [16] <dq>What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have hewn a burial-site here, as he who hews himself a burial-site on high, inscribing a resting place for himself in a rock?</dq> [17] <dq>See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is hurling you away, O man, and is firmly grasping you,</dq> [18] <dq>rolling you up tightly like a ball, into a wide land. There you are to die, and there your esteemed chariots are to be the shame of your master’s house.</dq> [19] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall drive you from your office, and you shall be ousted from your position.</dq> [20] <dq>And it shall be in that day, that <dn>I</dn> shall call <dn>My</dn> servant Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu.</dq> [21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> your robe on him, and strengthen him with your girdle, and give <dn>את</dn> your authority into his hand. And he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and to the house of Yehuḏah.</dq> [22] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall place <dn>את</dn> the key of the house of Daviḏ on his shoulder. And he shall open, and no one shuts; and shall shut, and no one opens.</dq> [23] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall fasten him like a peg in a steadfast place, and he shall become a throne of esteem to his father’s house.</dq> [24] <dq>And they shall hang on him all the weight of his father’s house, the offspring and the offshoots, all vessels of small quantity, from the cups to all the jars.</dq> [25] <dq>In that day,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘the peg that is fastened in the steadfast place shall be removed and be cut down and fall, and the burden that was on it shall be cut off. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Message Concerning Tsor
readings.subtitle: The Fall of the Crowning City
readings.text: [Isaiah 23:1] The message concerning Tsor. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it has been destroyed, without house, without harbour. From the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them. [2] Be silent, you inhabitants of the coastland, you merchants of Tsiḏon, who passed over the sea, they filled you. [3] And on great waters the grain of Shiḥor, the harvest of the River, was her increase. And she was a market-place for the nations. [4] Be ashamed, O Tsiḏon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, “I have not laboured, nor brought forth children; neither have I reared young men, brought up maidens.” [5] Like the report of Mitsrayim, they too are grieved at the report of Tsor. [6] Pass over to Tarshish; wail, you inhabitants of the coastland! [7] Is this your city of revelry, whose antiquity is from days of old, whose feet carried her far off to sojourn? [8] Who has counselled this against Tsor, the crowning city, whose merchants are chiefs, whose traders are the esteemed of the earth? [9] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has counselled it, to defile <dn>את</dn> the pride of all splendour, and to shame <dn>את</dn> all the esteemed of the earth. [10] Overflow through your land like the River, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no more strength. [11] <dn>He</dn> has stretched out <dn>His</dn> hand over the sea, <dn>He</dn> shook the reigns; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given a command against Kena‛an to destroy <dn>את</dn> its strongholds. [12] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Never again shall you exult, O you oppressed maiden daughter of Tsiḏon. Arise, pass over to Kittim, even there you shall find no rest.”</dq> [13] See the land of the Kasdim – this people did not exist. Ashshur founded it for wild beasts of the desert. They set up <dn>את</dn> their siege-towers, they demolished her palaces, and made her a ruin. [14] Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!

readings.title: Tsor's Restoration and Consecration
readings.subtitle: Forgotten for Seventy Years
readings.text: [Isaiah 23:15] And in that day it shall be that Tsor is forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one sovereign. At the end of seventy years it shall be to Tsor as in the song of the whore: [16] “Take a lyre, go about the city, you forgotten whore; make sweet playing, sing many songs, so that you might be remembered.” [17] And at the end of seventy years it shall be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> visits <dn>את</dn> Tsor. And she shall return to her harlot-fee and commit whoring with <dn>את</dn> all the reigns of the earth on the face of the soil. [18] And her goods and her harlot-fee shall be set apart for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, not treasured nor laid up, for her gain is for those who dwell before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to eat sufficiently, and for a choice covering.
